## Project Description

This project focuses on both the acclimation rate and capacity of Skistodiaptomus pallidus, a freshwater species of calanoid copepod. This project will take place in two different parts. In the first part we will compare CTmax data of a control group (16C) and a warm group (22C), as well as how this differs between two different populations; Oschner Pond and Centenniel Park. In the second part of this project we will do a transcriptomic analysis of the different populations and temperature treatments and compare the expression and regulation of certain genes by looking at differences in RNA.

## Questions, Objectives, Hypotheses

Questions:
1. How does the magnitude/capacity of acclimation compare across populations and treatments?
2. How does the rate of acclimation compare across populations and treatments?
3, Is there a significant difference in the frequencies of certain RNA strands across the different populations and treatments?

Objectives:
1. Measure the capacity to acclimate of the different populations and treatments of S. pallidus.
2. Measure the rate of acclimation of the different populations and treatments of S. pallidus.
 3.Determine relationships between the frequency of certain RNA strands in response to heat acclimation.

Hypothesis:
1. The warm acclimation group will have exhibit an acclimation response and will have a higher CTmax in comparison to the control group by the end of the experiment.
2. If the warm group exhibits an acclimation response there will be significant differences in RNA when comparing the warm group and the control group.
